criteria.semantics: A native <h1> to <h6> at the heading's level, whose text is its content: a heading names the section after it, and the levels nest without skipping.

keyboard.outcome: Passes it by: it is not a stop in the tab order.

keyboard.key: Screen reader heading keys (H, or the rotor)
keyboard.outcome: Move to the heading, and by level (1 to 6).

criteria.name: The heading's content, the same words as its visible text.

setting.statement: WHEN I set my text size to 200% I SEE the heading grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I zoom the page to 400% I SEE the heading wrap onto as many lines as it needs, with no horizontal scrolling.

check.statement: The face emits a native heading element at the node's level: <h2> for level 2.
The heading's text is its content, so what a screen reader lists is what I see.
A heading is not a control: nothing in it is a stop in the tab order.
WHEN I move by headings with a desktop screen reader (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) I HEAR the heading's text and I HEAR it identify itself as a heading at its level.
WHEN I list the page's headings I HEAR them in order, their levels nesting without a skip.
WHEN I swipe to the heading with a mobile screen reader (TalkBack, VoiceOver) I HEAR its text and the role of heading.

criteria.semantics: The heading's content as bold text, larger the higher its level (level 1 the largest), in fg on bg. Once GPUI exposes a tree: an AccessKit Heading node with its level (AXHeading on macOS, a Text control with HeadingLevel on Windows, a heading with its level on AT-SPI).

keyboard.outcome: Pass the heading by: it is no stop of its own; the controls before and after it are.

keyboard.key: Screen reader heading navigation (VoiceOver's rotor, Narrator's H, Orca's H)
keyboard.outcome: Moves to the heading, once there is a tree.

criteria.name: The heading's content.
criteria.role: Heading, level 1 to 6 (VoiceOver: heading level 2; Narrator: heading level 2; Orca: heading level 2).

setting.statement: WHEN I set the system text size to 200% (Windows' Accessibility, Text size; GNOME's Large Text or text scaling factor) I SEE the heading grow with it, with no loss of information.
WHEN I raise the display scale (macOS' Displays, Larger Text; Windows' Scale at 150% or 200%; GNOME's Scale at 200%) I SEE the heading drawn sharp and larger, whole and without overlapping.

WHEN I turn on the platform's high contrast (macOS' Increase contrast, a Windows contrast theme, the desktop portal's contrast) I SEE the window switch to the high-contrast palette by itself, the heading at 7:1.
WHEN I choose the high-contrast theme for the window I SEE the heading drawn in the high-contrast palette, every pair at 7:1.
WHEN I magnify the screen (macOS Zoom, Windows Magnifier, GNOME's Zoom) I SEE the heading whole and legible in the magnified view.

check.statement: A heading adds no stop of its own to the window's tab order.
I SEE the heading larger and bolder than the text after it, and a lower level smaller than a higher one.
WHEN I move by headings with VoiceOver (macOS), Narrator (Windows) or Orca (Linux) I HEAR the heading's text and its level.

announce.api: AXHeading with AXValue the level (AccessKit Role::Heading, level set).
ControlType Text with HeadingLevel HeadingLevel2, its content as the Name.
ATSPI_ROLE_HEADING, its level as the level attribute.

criteria.note: GPUI 0.2.2 exposes no accessibility tree (no AccessKit, NSAccessibility, UI Automation or AT-SPI provider), so every HEAR check is blocked by the toolkit, and so are the system text size and the platform's high contrast, which it does not report. GPUI's main branch has AccessKit (zed-industries/zed#56065), not yet released (gpui/README.md, "Accessibility tree"). Its SEE checks with a probe run on GPUI's test platform (gpui/src/native.rs, every_gpui_see_check_with_a_probe_holds), which no CI job runs yet; the rest are reported as not verified.
